resources.string: Ready. Open any app and its text is translated in place.
Babel needs two permissions before it can translate.
Lets Babel read the text on screen. Translation runs for as long as this service is on.
Lets Babel draw the translation over the original text.
Usually best left automatic. Set it when detection gets the language wrong — a page of English read as Japanese, say — and nothing is translated as a result.
Follows the system language. This is what text is translated into, not the language of this app.
The Babel accessibility service is not running. Manga mode reads the screen through it.
While this is on, recognised text leaves your device. Nothing else about Babel sends anything anywhere.
Saved key kept — leave blank to reuse it
Leave blank for a server on your own machine
Paste the authentication key from your DeepL account — nothing else. The address follows from the key, and a free-tier key is recognised by its :fx ending.
Any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, path included — usually ends in /v1/chat/completions. A hosted service must use https; a server of your own is reached over http on localhost.
The key was rejected. Check the API key.
Nothing at that address. Check the endpoint, path included.
The service refused the request — usually the model name.
The key works but has no quota left.
Could not reach it. Check the address and your connection.
The service answered with something unexpected.
Fill in the fields above first.
This engine cannot translate that language pair.
The attribution file could not be read from this build.
Comic recogniser installed — lettering is read accurately.

Manga mode works without this, but the general recogniser breaks vertical Japanese into the wrong columns and reads them out of order. The translation that comes back is fluent and unrelated to the original. The comic recogniser reads the lettering as written.
This connection may be charged by the megabyte.
The download did not finish. What arrived is kept, so trying again continues from there.
What arrived was not the expected file. Trying again is unlikely to help; this build may need updating.
The download stopped for an unexpected reason.
Manga mode needs Android 11 or later. This device is below that.
Text is being read and translated, but nothing can be drawn on top of it: Babel does not have permission to appear over other apps. The translations are being discarded.

In recent apps, long-press Babel and lock it, so cleaning skips it. When you do not need translation, switch it off above or with the quick settings tile instead of clearing the app. Battery: set Babel to unrestricted.
Automatic recovery is off. Run this once from a computer, and after a force stop opening Babel once switches the accessibility service back on:
It is already in quick settings.
This phone does not offer to add it from here. Add \"Babel\" by hand through Edit in the control centre.
Added. Pull down the control centre and tap Babel (the 文A icon) to pause or resume the switches above from anywhere. To remove it, tap Edit there.
Add it to pause or resume the switches above from anywhere, without opening Babel.
A phone cleaner turns accessibility off; lock Babel in recent apps to prevent it. Automatic recovery is on.
A phone cleaner turns accessibility off; lock Babel in recent apps to prevent it. Automatic recovery is off.
Paused — translations already shown stay until the page changes
Reads the screen as a picture, to translate text in images
Off — everything is translated on this device. On translates much better, at the cost of sending recognised text to the service you name.
